\section[la infancia]{la infancia — childhood}

\label{lesson:ES-C483-infancia}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for fast, then the Spanish for the variety.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la infancia}
\textbf{la infancia} — \textquotedblleft{}childhood\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Pasé la infancia en un pueblo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I spent my childhood in a village.}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{infancia} $\leftarrow$ Latin \emph{infantia}, \textquotedblleft{}inability to speak; early childhood\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB 2.1), from \emph{infans}, \textquotedblleft{}not speaking\textquotedblright{}: \emph{in-}, \textquotedblleft{}not\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{fari}, \textquotedblleft{}to speak\textquotedblright{} — a learned word. The young child was named as the one who cannot talk yet.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la infancia}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la infancia}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la infancia}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for fast, then the Spanish for the variety, then say \emph{la infancia} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la infancia mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Childhood\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la costumbre]{la costumbre — the custom, the habit}

\label{lesson:ES-C483-costumbre}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the variety, then the Spanish for childhood.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la costumbre}
\textbf{la costumbre} — \textquotedblleft{}the custom, the habit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Es costumbre comer tarde.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{It is the custom to eat late.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Tener la costumbre de} — to be in the habit of.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{costumbre} $\leftarrow$ Old Spanish \emph{costumne} (EtymDB 2.1), from Latin \emph{consuetudo}, \emph{consuetudinis}, \textquotedblleft{}custom, habit\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short) — inherited and much worn: the shortened ending became \emph{-mbre}, as \emph{hominem}, \textquotedblleft{}man\textquotedblright{}, became \emph{hombre}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la costumbre}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la costumbre}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la costumbre}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the variety, then the Spanish for childhood, then say \emph{la costumbre} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[la finalidad]{la finalidad — the purpose, the aim}

\label{lesson:ES-C483-finalidad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for childhood, then the Spanish for the custom.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la finalidad}
\textbf{la finalidad} — \textquotedblleft{}the purpose, the aim\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La finalidad del curso es hablar más.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The aim of the class is to speak more.}
\end{quote}

A formal word, common on forms and notices.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{finalidad} is built from \emph{final}, \textquotedblleft{}final\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{-idad}. \emph{Final} is Latin \emph{finalis}, from \emph{finis}, \textquotedblleft{}an end\textquotedblright{}: a purpose is the end you aim at.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la finalidad}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for childhood, then the Spanish for the custom, then say \emph{la finalidad} again
\end{itemize}

\section[la mejora]{la mejora — the improvement}

\label{lesson:ES-C483-mejora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the custom, then the Spanish for the purpose.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la mejora}
\textbf{la mejora} — \textquotedblleft{}the improvement\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Se nota la mejora en las notas.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{You can see the improvement in the marks.}
\end{quote}

The noun of \emph{mejorar}, to improve.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{mejora} is the noun of \emph{mejorar}, \textquotedblleft{}to improve\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{mejor}, \textquotedblleft{}better\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{melior} — inherited: the \emph{-li-} became \emph{j}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[acudir]{acudir — to go, to come (to a place or to someone for help)}

\label{lesson:ES-C483-acudir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the purpose, then the Spanish for the improvement.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: acudir}
\textbf{acudir} — \textquotedblleft{}to go, to come (to a place or to someone for help)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Acuda a la oficina con su pasaporte.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Come to the office with your passport.}
\end{quote}

Notices use it where speech would use \emph{ir} or \emph{venir}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{acudir} is usually explained as Old Spanish \emph{recudir}, \textquotedblleft{}to come back, to turn to\textquotedblright{}, with its prefix changed to \emph{a-}; \emph{recudir} is Latin \emph{recutere}, \textquotedblleft{}to strike back, to make rebound\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{acudir}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{acudir}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{acudir}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the purpose, then the Spanish for the improvement, then say \emph{acudir} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
